attachments.name: Staff Memo for Council 2024 Officer of the Year

description:
It is our honor today to recognize an individual whose actions have exemplified the highest standards of professionalism and dedication in the line of duty. The Officer of the Year Award is one of the highest honors we bestow upon a member of our department, and it is my privilege to present this award to someone who has gone above and beyond in a moment of life-or-death urgency.
After careful review of several nominations, it is with great pride that I announce Corporal Trinidad Gonzalez as the recipient of the Officer of the Year award for her extraordinary actions in saving a life.
On the morning of Tuesday, May 14, 2024, Corporal Gonzalez responded to a call from Miami-Dade County dispatch, reporting that a male was having difficulty breathing and had lost consciousness. The call was made by a friend of the individual, who was with him inside the apartment unit. Upon arriving at the scene, Cpl. Gonzalez was the first officer on site. Inside the condo unit, she found a 69-year-old male, unconscious, not breathing, and without a pulse. Without hesitation, Corporal Gonzalez immediately began CPR and informed dispatch that she was starting chest compressions. Her swift and decisive actions in that critical moment were nothing short of heroic.
As Cpl. Gonzalez worked tirelessly by providing lifesaving aid for over five minutes, Miami-Dade Fire Rescue arrived and took over the scene. Thanks to her quick thinking and skilled application of the CPR techniques she learned through the department's training, the male regained a pulse. He was subsequently transported to Mount Sinai Hospital by Fire Rescue, where he received further medical care.
Cpl. Gonzalez’s immediate response and her dedication to putting her training into action directly contributed to saving a life. Her actions not only reflect the skills and knowledge we work so hard to develop but also the compassion and commitment to service that make our officers true heroes in the community.
Today, we honor Corporal Trinidad Gonzalez for her courage, professionalism, and quick thinking. It is because of officers like her that we are reminded of the significant impact we have as public servants. Cpl. Gonzalez, on behalf of the department and the community you serve, thank you for your exceptional service and for embodying the very best of what it means to be a law enforcement officer.
Please join me in congratulating Corporal Trinidad Gonzalez as the Officer of the Year for the Bay Harbor Islands Police Department and also as recipient of the Life Saving Award. Your actions have made a lasting difference, and we are proud to recognize your incredible work.
title: BHIPD 2024 Officer of The Year

CMA Proposal to Design Block 11 Water Mians

description:
Purchase Order (PO) # 042122 is associated with Project # BHI 223 which was issued to perform civil engineering designs for the Block 11 Alleyway Construction. The Block 11 Alleyway is currently on privately owned property and as a result will be relocated to property owned by the Town of Bay Harbor Islands. The design and permitting of the Alleyway Construction are about 95% completed.
The Block 11 Water Main Replacement project, identified as BHI 262, is for the relocation of the Town-owned 6” water main that is in the alleyway. The new water main must be within the boundaries of the relocated alleyway and, therefore, the relocation of the alleyway and the relocation of the water main ought to have been established as one project as there is duplication of effort if they’re done separately. Moreover, if they must be separated, the water main designs should be completed first, as the new water main would have to be laid before the alleyway is constructed.
As a result of the inextricable link between the alleyway construction and the water mains, CMA was requested to provide a cost estimate to also design water mains within the relocated alleyway and their proposal is attached, in the amount of $63,520.00.
Although it clearly was the intention to award the Block 11 Water Main design to another consultant (and hence its unique Project number), it is my professional opinion, there is engineering and economic value in combining these two projects and giving it to one consultant. As a result, I am requesting that the original PO # 042122 be amended in the amount of $63,520.00 to include the design of Block 11 Water Main in the design for the Block 11 Alleyway.
As a result of previously conducted surveys, if this PO modification is approved, CMA will immediately commence water mains designs and are expected to deliver the completed design package for both the Block 11 Alleyway (BHI 223) and Water mains (BHI 262) in 6 weeks.
However, permitting by the Florida Department of Environmental Protection (FDEP) and other regulatory agencies may require 8–16 weeks before the project may be publicly advertised for construction bids. Although it may be possible to fast track permitting, construction bid documents may still not be ready until July-August 2025.

description:
Staff recommends that the Town Council approve the contract with RedSpeed for the installation, operation, and maintenance of the School Red Light Camera System, as outlined in the attached agreement. The contract includes provisions for RedSpeed to install the necessary equipment, manage ongoing operations, and provide support services for the system designed to enhance traffic safety in school zones.
On March 5, 2025, the Town Council approved an ordinance establishing the School Red Light Camera System to increase safety for students, parents, and pedestrians in school zones. This initiative was based on data gathered from a traffic study which highlighted significant speeding violations in the areas around Ruth K. Broad Bay Harbor K-8 Center, particularly along Kane Concourse (96th Street) and West Bay Harbor Drive. To implement this system, the Town sought proposals from qualified vendors, and after a competitive process, RedSpeed was selected as the contractor.
RedSpeed, a reputable provider of traffic enforcement systems, has agreed to provide a comprehensive solution that includes the installation of speed detection cameras, ongoing maintenance, violation processing services, and public awareness initiatives.
The contract with RedSpeed covers the following key elements:
Turnkey Solution
RedSpeed will deliver a fully operational School Red Light Camera System, managing all aspects of system implementation and operation, excluding specific tasks identified as the Town’s responsibility (see “Town Scope of Work”).
Installation and Maintenance
RedSpeed will install the camera systems at designated intersections and school zone areas, including Kane Concourse (96th Street) and West Bay Harbor Drive. These locations will be prioritized based on the traffic study data. Additional locations may be added at the Town’s discretion. RedSpeed will also be responsible for all associated permits, signage, and electrical work. The systems will be operational 24 hours a day, except during scheduled maintenance and servicing.
Violation Processing and Data Access
RedSpeed will provide a secure web portal (www.SpeedViolations.com) where vehicle owners can view violation images and videos. The portal will meet all current Americans with Disabilities Act (ADA) requirements. RedSpeed will process violations, send notices, and provide customer service through a dedicated call center. The system will include a secure demand deposit account for the collection and transfer of funds to the Town’s bank account.
System Maintenance and Performance
RedSpeed will perform monthly preventive maintenance checks, including cleaning camera lenses, inspecting system components, and calibrating equipment annually per Florida statutes. If a system malfunctions, RedSpeed will make best efforts to repair the system within 48 hours, ensuring no violations are recorded during downtime. The system will not be inoperative for more than five days.
Public Awareness and Support
RedSpeed will assist with a public awareness campaign, including multilingual PSA materials, printed handouts, posters, and social media support to educate the community about the new system. A 30-day warning period will be implemented, during which violators will only receive warnings, not fines. During this period, the Town will distribute flyers and other materials to raise awareness.
Citations and Enforcement
RedSpeed will provide an automated citation processing system (RedCheck) that includes image processing, printing, and mailing of violation notices. The system will be integrated with vehicle registration databases to issue citations in compliance with state law. RedSpeed will also assist with adjudication processing, allowing the Town to review and dispute violations online.
Cost and Revenue Share
The Town will pay RedSpeed a fee based on 35% of the Town’s statutory share of collected revenue from traffic citations. RedSpeed will provide all necessary equipment, maintenance, and operational services as part of this fee, ensuring that no additional costs are incurred by the Town unless specifically authorized in writing.
Additional Services
RedSpeed will provide on-demand video, reports, and custom reports tailored to the Town’s needs, at no additional charge. The system will include a help desk for Town staff and a call center for violators, ensuring timely support and troubleshooting.
System Relocation
RedSpeed will relocate the camera systems at no cost to the Town if agreed upon, ensuring flexibility in response to changing enforcement needs.
The contract with RedSpeed covers an initial term of five (5) years, with the option for the Town to extend it for additional terms. The contract stipulates that all costs related to system installation, maintenance, and operation are covered by RedSpeed, with the revenue-sharing model ensuring the Town’s financial interest is protected. Payments to RedSpeed will be made monthly, based on the collected revenue from citations.
The approval of the contract with RedSpeed will allow the Town to implement the School Red Light Camera System, which is critical for improving safety in school zones around Ruth K. Broad Bay Harbor K-8 Center. The system will help deter speeding violations and enhance overall traffic safety. RedSpeed’s comprehensive services, including installation, maintenance, violation processing, and public awareness support, will ensure the system operates efficiently and effectively.
Staff recommend that the Town Council approve the contract with RedSpeed to install and operate the School Red Light Camera System. This contract represents a proactive step toward improving traffic safety in the Town and ensuring a safer environment for students and pedestrians.

Consequently, staff was directed to approach other consultants to design this Park.

On 04/04/2025, CMA provided a revised proposal to design the Park in the amount of $121,875.00. CMA submitted a time frame of 11 weeks to produce complete design plans.
The final scope of work for the project consists of the following:
1. Lockable kayak storage for as many kayaks as could fit. The storage unit shall be enclosed on the southern, western and eastern sides.
2. 10-foot x 10-foot shade structure on a concrete slab
3. Floating dock with electric lifts for handicapped people and their kayaks
4. 5-foot concrete walkway
5. Drop off zone along West Bay Harbor Drive
6. A lockable entry gate
7. New landscaping on the northern, southern, and western boundaries of the property
8. A wash area for people
9. A wash area for Kayaks
10. Irrigation system
11. On site stormwater retention area
12. Sod site with St. Augustine
A shade structure will allow a more cost-effective design option than a gazebo. A gazebo requires specific structural designs which will incur additional design fees.

Staff recommends that the Town Council approve an agreement with Momentum Marketing Group Corp. for the organization and production of the Bay Harbor Islands Art Festival, at the amount selected by the Town Council. This agreement will enable the successful planning and execution of the event, ensuring its alignment with the Town's goals and objectives.
The Town's Art Festival has been a successful annual event for the past three years, attracting large crowds and showcasing local talent. As we approach the fourth year, it's important to select a reliable vendor to manage event planning, logistics, and artist coordination to continue delivering a high-quality experience.
The timeline of the solicitation process includes the following:

The Evaluation Committee met with the procurement specialist to evaluate the proposal submitted by Momentum Marketing Group Corp. After review and analysis, the Committee determined that this proposal was both responsible and responsive.
The proposed vendor stands out for several key reasons:
1. Proven Experience: They've successfully managed our past three Art Festivals, understanding our needs and delivering consistently high-quality results.
2. Comprehensive Services: The vendor handles all aspects of the event, from logistics to vendor management, ensuring seamless execution.
3. Community Engagement: They prioritize local artists and foster community involvement, receiving positive feedback from past participants and attendees.
4. Reputation: Known for reliability and professionalism, they've consistently met deadlines and stayed within budget.
5. Cost-Effective: Their proposal is competitive, offering good value for the services provided.
If the Town Council approves the attached resolution, the Town Manager will execute an agreement with Momentum Marketing Group Corp to complete the project as outlined in the Request of Proposals at a price not to exceed $225,000.

description:
The Town has historically entered into Parking Lease Agreements to allow buildings with no onsite parking to utilize Town right-of-way parking for residents of those buildings.
Pursuant to Section 23-25 of the Town Code of Ordinances, the Town Council is to determine the license fee for the right-of-way parking. A $20 per parking space fee is currently charged for the existing parking lease agreements. In order to consider modification of pricing for these lease agreements, the Town Council would first need to increase its license fee schedule. Additionally, to increase the parking lease license fee for a particular licensee, the Town would first have to terminate the existing parking lease license agreement and then enter into a new parking lease license agreement with the new parking lease license fee. The standard parking lease license agreement allows the Town to terminate upon giving 30 days advance written notice following a public hearing.
Currently, most of the Town’s existing parking lease license agreements have auto-renewal provisions, so the Town will need to take affirmative action to terminate these agreements and modify the agreement as desired, in order to implement any needed changes for the lease agreements.
If the Town Council directs staff to bring forth changes in the parking lease license agreements, these lease agreements will not be renewed until the Council takes affirmative action to adopt proposed changes.
